new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Acrobat PDFMaker 2004-09-05, title 'OPD', author 'SIL PNG Branch'), its extracted text dump, and the rendered page image. Page 3 (header 'Suau OPD Printed: September 6, 2004 Page 3') carries the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' followed by the three numbered points exactly as quoted, including the typo 'syllabel' in point 2 and the wording 'If anywhere, the strongest stress tends to be on the last accented syllable' in point 3; the only differences are line-wrap positions. The 'Stress Examples' block is there with the eight forms ('s 'nom; 'ss 'lu.bi; 'ss'ss 'di.li.'wa.ʔu; 'ss's-s 'ga.gi.'li.-na; 'ss's-s 'nu.a.-'pou.gu; 's'ss 'tau.-'ba.ba; 's's-s 'lam.-'lam-na; 'ss-'s-'s 'ma…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Heavy syllables (containing a vowel sequence VV or a coda consonant VC) are always stressed. Among light syllables, stress falls on every odd-numbered syllable counting from the left (1st, 3rd..), restarting after a heavy syllable; a light final syllable is never stressed. The strongest (primary) stress is on the rightmost stressed syllable. Examples: 'nom 'to drink'; 'lu.bi 'to hit'; 'di.li.'wa.ʔu 'ceremonial axe'; 'ga.gi.'li.-na 'small'; 'nu.a.-'pou.gu 'to run'; 'tau.-'ba.ba 'big man, sir'; 'lam.-'lam-na 'its roots'; 'ma.la.'tom-'tom 'in the morning'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Implicit: multiple stresses per word are marked ('every odd syllable' plus every heavy syllable); the source says only that 'the strongest stress tends to be on the last accented syllable', so the earlier stresses are in effect secondary. No explicit term 'secondary stress' is used.
new_statements.exceptions: Heavy syllables 'throw the pattern off' (alternation restarts after them); hedged wording ('normally', 'tends to'). No lexical exceptions listed. Tone and length: heading covers them but nothing further is said (no tone; no vowel length noted).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word, including suffixed forms (e.g. -na 'its', -gu 'my' shown with hyphens); citation forms in a phoneme list; no phrase-level statement. Source is an undated SIL 'Organised Phonology Data' draft compiled from earlier fieldwork (Cooper, Capell, Pawley, Lynch) and one speaker, not a peer-reviewed description.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD header names the Fife Bay Subdistrict area, villages Ilo'ilo, Bonalua, Modeiwa, Sibalai, Suau, Sawaia, Saga'aho, Isu'isu, Isudau, Awalolo, Se'ase'a, Silosilo (mainland Suau coast from Fife Bay to Suau Island, plus Bonarua), i.e. 'Standard Suau' = Glottolog Nuclear Suau [nucl1500] and Bonarua [bona1252] dialects of suau1242; the recorded speaker is from Modeiwa. Suau is also the Kwato mission lingua franca; the OPD's data are not the Daui [daui1237] or Sinaki/Gadaisu [sina1264] varieties.
